 This Writ Petition Is Filed Under Articles 226

Quash The Preliminary Notification Issued By The R-2
Dated 8.4.2003 Vide Ann-G, Final Notification Dated
9.9.2003 Vide Ann-H Issued By The R -1 And The
Possession Mahazar Dated 24.11.2003 Issued By The
R-4 Special Land Acquisition Officer Vide Ann-Q
Respectively By Giving Effect To The Provisions Of
Section 24[2] Of Right To Fair Compensation And
Transparency In Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation
And Resettlement Act 2013 And Etc.,
 This Petition Coming On For Final Hearing This
Day, The Court Made The Following:-
 Order

Petitioner is knocking at the doors of Writ Court for assailing the acquisition proceedings in respect of the subject land pursuant to Preliminary Notification dated 08.04.2003 issued by the 1st Respondent - Government at Annexure-G under Section 17 of the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976.

It is the case of the Petitioner that the acquisition proceedings having not been accomplished within statutory period of five years in terms of Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013,
the same are liable to be quashed.

sentences.text: 2. After service of notice, the State appears through the learned AGA; BDA and its officials are represented by their Sr. Panel Counsel.

Both they oppose the Writ Petition contending that the acquisition having been done under the provisions of 1976 Act, there is no scope for invoking the provisions of Section 24(2) of 2013 Act for invalidating the acquisition proceedings.

In support of the same, they rely upon the decision of the Apex Court in BANGALORE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY & ANOTHER vs THE STATE OF KARNATAKA & OTHERS, (2018) 9 SCC 122.
3.

Admittedly, the acquisition in question was under the provisions of the 1976 Act and not under the provisions of the erstwhile Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
